posts.post_subject: Need help choosing Q-switch and Doubler, Pulsed Holography
posts.content_md:
Hello Holographers,

I am in the process of building up an inexpensive 532nm pulsed holography setup. It is based on old parts from the flashlamp pumped medical lasers we make at work. 2600 microfarads at up to 1000 VDC to the flash lamp, gated by a solid state IGBT handling 1200V at 600A max. Flash the lamp for about 160 microseconds. Electronics automatically trigger and simmer the flashlamp so it is easy to dump the charge to the lamp at the appropriate time. The rod is Nd:YAG, 5mm diameter. Need to select a (passive Cr4+:YAG ?) q-switch crystal to handle ~500MW/cm2, 10-50ns pulses, with proper initial transmittance, which I can't figure out. Also need to know HR and OC transmittance / reflectance, and coatings. Then frequency double the 5mm diameter 1064nm beam to 532nm (KDP or KTP ?).

Anyone know how to calculate these components? I am weaker on optics than the electronics. Have optical / electronic parts to swap so you can do tests too. Need a source of the crystals for testing. Any interest would be appreciated.

Sincerely,

Bill Jensen

Reverse Engineering.

That is, why not call, write or look on a web site for a reputable manufacturer of a pulsed NdYag system that can be used for holography and pick their brain or search their site with the interest of a pulsed Frequency Doubled system for holography. This should tell you they type of FD and q-switch they use.

Hi there,

Thank you for your responses. It looks like I have the use of Tom's KTP crystals. If I get mine working, it will allow me to know what I can do to his 20W Laserscope to make it pulsed Holography compatible.

I am reading the articles mentioned, and slowly looking for the Holography Marketplace articles by Ron Olsen on Pulsed Holography. I met Ron and Bernadette about 10 years ago in their San Jose studio, and became interested in Holography then. I have sent a question or two to them by email.

I got initially messed up by the formula: Joules equals one half capacitance in farads times the voltage squared. This seems to apply to caps charged up and fully dumping into a flash lamp. What I have is an IGBT dumping only a part of the energy for say 160 microseconds time into the flashlamp, so this formula does not work. Looking for the correct formula. Is it Power in Watts = I x V and Watts = Joules x sec?

Sincerely,

Bill Jensen

> **Bill Jensen:** Hi there,so this formula does not work. Looking for the correct formula. Is it Power in Watts = I x V and Watts = Joules x sec?Sincerely,Bill Jensen

Energy = power x the time over which the power operates

so Joules = watts x secs

so as a matter of interest a 1 joule pulsed laser can be a dangerous 

beast because in a 10 nanosec pulse (10-8sec)

Power = watts = 1/10-8 = 100million watts!

No wonder it blows holes in your aluminized mirrors and ionizes the air

if you put it through even a mild convex lens.

jeff
